premises.text: Passwords create a human weak link, and existing SSO/IAM/password tools either demand heavy IT adoption or centralize secrets in the cloud as a single point of failure
premises.evidence_span: over 86% of breaches today are caused by users and not by hackers

premises.text: MyKey lets users authenticate from the phone with biometrics while admins share, revoke, privilege-limit, geo/time/IP-rule, and rotate passwords without service-provider integrations
premises.evidence_span: fundamentally changing the way teams manage access to the digital workspace

premises.text: Initial go-to-market targets medium companies with 10–50 users at free-for-five then about $4.99 per additional user per month, with later upmarket custom integrations and on-prem
premises.evidence_span: initially targeting medium-sized companies that have between 10 and 50 users

value.text: Secure team access to the digital workspace without complicated, expensive security tooling
value.evidence_span: security doesn't have to be something complicated, expensive, and time consuming

causal_links.evidence_span: All of these tools put your sensitive information in the cloud, creating a single point of failure
MyKey is free for the first five users and then starts at $5, $4.99 per additional user per month

notes: User login push, admin portal, privilege levels, geo/time/IP rules, background password change, and no-integration claim folded as cascade of one access-management mechanism (§4.1.7). Early-customer traction and team credentials excluded. Anti-template: problem, product, and SMB pricing/GTM are separately revisable.
